alt: Starting from the claimant’s loss, damages pass three filters: causation (the breach must be an effective cause; Quinn v Burch Brothers), remoteness (Hadley v Baxendale, judged at the time of contracting) and mitigation (British Westinghouse). What remains is recoverable as of right, compensatory, not punitive.
caption: Loss is reduced by causation, remoteness and mitigation before damages are paid.

alt: Six categories: expectation loss (Robinson v Harman), reliance loss (Anglia Television v Reed), loss of a chance (Chaplin v Hicks), loss of amenity where cure is disproportionate (Ruxley v Forsyth, £2,500), and non-pecuniary loss, generally barred (Addis) but recoverable where pleasure or peace of mind is a major object (Jarvis; Farley v Skinner).
caption: Expectation is the default; the others fill gaps where it cannot be measured.

alt: Hadley v Baxendale’s two limbs: losses arising naturally (with The Heron II’s “not unlikely” test) and losses in both parties’ contemplation because of special knowledge, judged at contracting. Cases: Hadley (lost mill profits too remote), Victoria Laundry (ordinary profits recovered, lucrative contracts not), Parsons v Uttley Ingham (type contemplated, full extent recovered) and The Achilleas (assumption of responsibility).
caption: What the defendant knew when contracting sets the limit of liability.

alt: Specific performance orders the contract to be carried out where damages are inadequate: granted for land, unique goods (Falcke v Gray) and in Beswick v Beswick; refused for personal service, constant supervision (Co-operative Insurance v Argyll), severe hardship (Patel v Ali) or unfairness and delay. Rescission sets the contract aside for misrepresentation or economic duress, and is lost by affirmation, lapse of time, third-party rights or impossible restitution.
caption: Both depend on the court’s discretion, unlike damages.

alt: Termination is available for breach of a condition (Poussard v Spiers), a serious breach of an innominate term (Hong Kong Fir; not The Hansa Nord) or renunciation. The innocent party elects to terminate, ending future obligations with damages for the lost bargain, or to affirm. Rescission undoes a contract from the start; termination ends it for the future. Consumers have statutory rights to reject under the Consumer Rights Act 2015.
caption: Termination ends the future; rescission unwinds the past.

alt: Leah’s wedding profit of £6,000 is not too remote because Ovenco was told (Victoria Laundry); the unmentioned £9,000 banquet profit is too remote. A similar oven was available for £11,000 on 10 April, so under Payzu v Saunders a court may limit damages to the £1,000 extra cost rather than £6,000. Specific performance is irrelevant.
caption: Remoteness removes the banquet; mitigation may shrink the rest to £1,000.
